nodes.description: A slowly inactivating potassium-current deficit is measured in LGI1-deficient cultured mouse CA3 neurons. LGI1 restoration and Kv1 blockade support its contribution to altered excitability in this preparation.

evidence.reference_title: Rescue of Normal Excitability in LGI1-Deficient Epileptic Neurons.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that the selective expression of LGI1 in KO-Lgi1 neurons from mice of both sexes, using single-cell electroporation, reduces intrinsic excitability and restores both the Kv1.1-mediated D-type current and Kv1.1 channels at the AIS.

experimental_models.description: Local LGI1 expression restores the DTx-K-sensitive conductance; toxin reapplication supports a channel contribution to intrinsic rescue.

nodes.description: Selected pathogenic LGI1 variants reduce extracellular availability through abnormal folding, intracellular retention or degradation. E383A is one experimentally characterized example; secretion-competent pathogenic variants also occur.

nodes.description: Selected epilepsy-associated mutant reelin proteins show impaired trafficking and reduced secretion in transfected-cell assays. A loss of extracellular function is a proposed epileptogenic mechanism, without direct measurement of the corresponding patient brain pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Epilepsy-causing Reelin mutations result in impaired secretion and intracellular degradation of mutant proteins.
evidence.snippet: Using a cell-based secretion assay, we show that pathogenic RELN mutations abolish or significantly reduce secretion of mutant proteins and that this secretion defect results from impaired trafficking of mutant Reelin along the secretory pathway.

experimental_models.description: Mutant-protein secretion is reduced in the reported assay.

nodes.description: Treat focal seizures with an antiseizure medication selected by an experienced neurologist for seizure type, comorbidity, interactions and reproductive considerations. Carbamazepine has historically been used with benefit, but comparative ADEAF-specific trials do not establish a uniquely preferred drug. Many patients respond to monotherapy; persistent seizures and withdrawal decisions require reassessment.
